subject: Edström et al. (1990)
object: Edström et al. (1990) described 16 patients from 7 pedigrees with an unusual adult-onset limb-girdle myopathy. All patients had prominent early respiratory muscle weakness, and in many an acute respiratory incapacity prompted the first neurologic examination. Neck flexor weakness and sometimes foot extensor weakness were other early symptoms. Electrophysiologic analysis confirmed a myopathy, and serum muscle enzyme levels were normal or slightly elevated.

subject: Edström et al. (1990)
object: Edström et al. (1990) found evidence of autosomal dominant inheritance in the majority of the 16 patients from 7 pedigrees with myopathy and early respiratory failure.

subject: Edström et al. (1990)
object: Edström et al. (1990) found myofibrillar changes on muscle biopsy, including plaques that stained strongly with rhodamine-conjugated phalloidin, a marker for F-actin. Ultrastructurally, the plaques were composed of moderately dense thin filaments and were related to splitting of Z-discs or formed extensions from Z-discs.

subject: Edström et al. (1990)
object: Edström et al. (1990) suggested that the muscle biopsy changes indicated defective myofibrillogenesis and discussed the possibility of defective actin polymerization.

subject: Nicolao et al. (1999)
object: Nicolao et al. (1999) studied 2 Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy. Affected members had proximal weakness and early respiratory failure, and their muscle biopsies showed characteristic cytoplasmic bodies.

subject: Nicolao et al. (1999)
object: Nicolao et al. (1999) ran a genome-wide linkage screen in 2 Swedish families and mapped the disease to chromosome 2q24-q31. They obtained a maximum combined two-point LOD score of 4.87 at theta = 0 with marker D2S1245. Haplotype analysis placed the gene in a 17-cM region between D2S2384 and D2S364.

subject: Nicolao et al. (1999)
object: Nicolao et al. (1999) found that affected individuals from the 2 Swedish families shared an identical haplotype, which suggested a common origin.

subject: Xiang et al. (1999)
object: Xiang et al. (1999) studied a French family with autosomal dominant myopathy. The family's clinical phenotype and muscle biopsy findings were similar to those of the Swedish families with proximal muscle weakness and early respiratory muscle involvement mapped to 2q24-q31. However, the 2q24-q31 region was completely excluded in the French family.

subject: Xiang et al. (1999)
object: Xiang et al. (1999) performed a genome-wide scan with polymorphic microsatellite markers in the French family. They obtained a maximum two-point lod score of 2.11, the highest achievable in this family, for markers in a 4-cM region between D2S1272 and D2S1260. The authors suggested that the gene for the French form is likely located on chromosome 2q21.

subject: Chinnery et al. (2001)
object: Chinnery et al. (2001) described a novel autosomal dominant myopathy in a 3-generation family. Affected members presented in mid-adult life with weakness of the tibialis anterior. The authors clinically assessed 24 individuals, 11 of whom were affected. Affected members of the second generation presented at an earlier age, and their disease progressed more rapidly than in the first generation. Weakness of the hip girdle and shoulder girdle appeared later in the course.

subject: Chinnery et al. (2001)
object: In this family, Chinnery et al. (2001) found on lung function testing a progressive global weakness of the respiratory muscles that could be detected from the time of presentation. In some cases the diaphragm was preferentially involved.

subject: Chinnery et al. (2001)
object: Chinnery et al. (2001) studied muscle pathology in 7 of the 11 affected individuals, including 1 at autopsy, and found that pathology correlated closely with clinical involvement. Muscles that were clinically unaffected showed minimal change. Moderately affected muscles showed fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and rimmed vacuoles with basophilic rims. In severely involved muscles, the muscle fibers had been replaced by fat and fibrous connective tissue. The inclusions were Congophilic and reacted with antibodies to desmin, beta-amyloid, and phosphorylated tau protein.

subject: Chinnery et al. (2001)
object: Chinnery et al. (2001) found that the disease in this family was not linked to any of the known loci associated with distal myopathies. They concluded that the disorder is genetically and phenotypically distinct.

subject: Lange et al. (2005)
object: Lange et al. (2005) identified a signaling complex in which the titin protein kinase domain (TK) interacts with the zinc-finger protein nbr1 through a mechanically inducible conformation. Nbr1 targets the ubiquitin-associated protein p62/SQSTM1 to sarcomeres. p62 in turn interacts with MuRF2, a muscle-specific RING-B-box E3 ligase that binds the transactivation domain of serum response factor (SRF).

subject: Lange et al. (2005)
object: Lange et al. (2005) found that mechanical inactivity induced MuRF2 to move into the nucleus. This reduced nuclear SRF and repressed transcription, which suggests that the titin kinase domain controls muscle gene expression and protein turnover in response to mechanical load.

subject: Lange et al. (2005)
object: Lange et al. (2005) reported that a human mutation in the titin (TTN) protein kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting the TK–nbr1–p62–MuRF2 signaling pathway.

subject: Birchall et al. (2005)
object: Birchall et al. (2005) performed muscle MRI on 7 patients (age range 37-66 years, 4 male) with autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure, a dominant limb myopathy with insidious onset in late adult life in which respiratory failure occurs while patients are still ambulant. MRI showed selective early involvement of the semitendinosus and obturator externus muscles that could not be detected clinically, with different rates of progression in closely related muscles.

subject: Birchall et al. (2005)
object: Birchall et al. (2005) concluded that subclinical semitendinosus and obturator externus involvement on muscle MRI is specific to autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure and enables early noninvasive diagnosis of at-risk individuals, which is otherwise difficult because of the insidious late-adult onset and highly selective clinical and pathologic muscle involvement.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2012)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2012) used genome-wide linkage combined with whole exome sequencing in a family with autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure and identified a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2 containing the likely causal variant in TTN.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2012)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2012) identified a variant in the TTN gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg) that segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, 9 subjects in a second family with the same selective pattern of muscle involvement on MRI, and a third familial case with a similar phenotype.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2012)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2012) defined the phenotype in 31 TTN mutation carriers followed for up to 31 years. Presentation included predominant distal, proximal, or respiratory muscle weakness, with highly variable age of onset from early adulthood to a mild phenotype in advanced age; weakness was earlier and more severe in the lower extremities in nearly all patients, 7 had axial weakness, respiratory function deteriorated gradually over time, and no patient had cardiomyopathy.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2012)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2012) performed muscle MRI in 21 affected patients and found characteristic abnormalities with semitendinosus involvement in 20 of 21, including 3 presymptomatic patients. Muscle histopathology most frequently showed eosinophilic inclusions (inclusion bodies) and rimmed vacuoles but was nonspecific in a minority.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2012)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2012) suggested that the disease be considered in patients with adult-onset proximal or distal myopathy and early respiratory failure, even with nonspecific pathology, that muscle MRI be an initial investigation prompting TTN screening if positive, and that whole exome sequencing provides a reliable cost-effective approach to screening the 363-exon TTN gene.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2014)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2014) screened 127 unrelated UK probands with undiagnosed myopathy compatible with myofibrillar myopathy (MFM) by Sanger sequencing of the 119th FN3 domain and part of the kinase domain of TTN. The heterozygous g.274375T>C (p.C30071R) mutation was found in 5 of 127 (3.9%) probands, including 4 of 72 with a clinical diagnosis of MFM (5.5%); it cosegregated with disease in families F.1, F.2, and F.4. No patients had mutations at p.32450 in the kinase domain.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2014)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2014) described 11 patients from 5 British families with the TTN p.C30071R mutation. Onset was typically in the fourth or fifth decade with tripping, falling, myalgia and walking difficulty; CK ranged from normal to 1195 IU/L; the course was slowly progressive with proximal, distal and axial involvement, and only 1 patient lost ambulation after about 25 years. Ten of 11 had abnormal pulmonary function indicating respiratory muscle weakness, and 4 required nocturnal noninvasive ventilation 20 to 30 years after onset. Newly noted features included often asymmetric scapular winging, elbow and/or Achilles tendon contractures, variable spinal rigidity, and muscle hypertrophy; cardiac involvement was mild left ventricular impairment in 1 and supraventricular tachycardia in 1.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2014)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2014) reported muscle MRI in 3 patients with the p.C30071R mutation showing early involvement of the semitendinosus and peroneus longus muscles, including a presymptomatic individual.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2014)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2014) found that muscle biopsies of p.C30071R patients showed myopathic or dystrophic changes; rimmed vacuoles in 3, eosinophilic and dark blue Gomori trichrome inclusions in 3, and cytoplasmic accumulation of desmin, myotilin, p62 and ubiquitin in 6 of 7 biopsies. Three biopsies showed cytoplasmic aggregates with a 'cheetah skin' appearance, particularly with myotilin staining, and inclusions did not fully overlap with protein accumulations. The authors concluded these features supported a diagnosis of MFM.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2014)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2014) found that probands of 5 new families and 3 previously reported families with p.C30071R shared a common core haplotype of 171 kb on chromosome 2; the probability of this sharing in 8 unrelated families by chance was less than 10(-6). The small shared region suggested an ancient mutation, and the authors attributed the frequency of the mutation (5.5% of undiagnosed UK MFM patients) to a British founder effect.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2014)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2014) identified a novel heterozygous TTN variant, g.274436C>T (p.P30091L), at a highly conserved residue in the 119th FN3 domain, in a patient (F.6) with adult-onset MFM-compatible myopathy with proximal weakness, mild neck weakness, calf hypertrophy, scapular winging, respiratory involvement (FVC 52%), and biopsy showing rimmed vacuoles and myotilin/p62 accumulation. The variant was absent from 400 control chromosomes but was also carried by a healthy 61-year-old brother, suggesting it may be neutral, although reduced penetrance could not be excluded.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2014)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2014) identified a novel heterozygous TTN variant, g.274599C>G (p.N30145K), in the 119th FN3 domain in a patient from Brazil (F.7) with adult-onset proximal limb weakness, severe ankle dorsiflexion weakness, scapular winging, and several affected relatives who were unavailable. MRI showed semitendinosus, tibialis anterior and peroneus longus involvement, and biopsy showed rimmed vacuoles and cytoplasmic bodies. The variant was absent from 400 control chromosomes; segregation could not be assessed.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2014)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2014) proposed that hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure (HMERF) due to TTN mutations be classified nosologically as MFM-titinopathy.

subject: Pfeffer et al. (2014)
object: Pfeffer et al. (2014) recommended sequencing the 119th FN3 domain of TTN in the diagnostic workup of MFM, particularly with early respiratory involvement and supportive muscle MRI, and recommended cardiac surveillance for patients with TTN mutations. They cautioned that TTN is highly polymorphic, with 71 novel coding variants found in exome data from 239 subjects, none in the 119th FN3 domain.
